purpose: Provide a subdomain knowledge node, within a knowledge-searcher meta-KB, for locating, applying, evaluating, and synthesizing the methods, decisions, and tradeoffs of philosophy of science and the epistemology of inquiry (inference modes, demarcation, confirmation, paradigm change, realism debates, explanation, and values).
assumptions: subdomain of research_methodology_and_epistemology, scoped to the epistemology of scientific inquiry
no observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
nodes are concrete, evaluable work units / methods / decision areas, not historical surveys
primary anchors include Popper (1959) and Kuhn (1962) plus standard secondary literature
exclusions: object-level results of particular sciences (physics, biology) themselves
general (non-scientific) epistemology of perception/testimony beyond inquiry
philosophy of mathematics and formal logic proper except as inference tools
empirical sociology/history of science beyond what bears on appraisal

competency_questions.question: What is the inquiry's epistemic aim and which authoritative sources ground it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EPISTEMIC_AIMS and RETRIEVAL_AND_SOURCING present with explicit aim/source criteria

competency_questions.question: Which mode of inference (inductive, deductive, abductive) is appropriate for a given claim?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDUCTION_PROBLEM, DEDUCTION_VALIDITY, ABDUCTION_IBE present and related

competency_questions.question: How is inductive risk assessed when generalizing from evidence?
By what criterion is a claim judged scientific vs pseudoscientific?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMARCATION and FALSIFICATIONISM present with criterion justification

competency_questions.question: How is a theory appraised after surviving (or failing) tests?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FALSIFICATIONISM, CORROBORATION, RESEARCH_PROGRAMMES present with appraisal logic

competency_questions.question: How does evidence quantitatively or qualitatively confirm a hypothesis?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFIRMATION_THEORY and BAYESIAN_EPISTEMOLOGY present with paradox handling

competency_questions.question: Does predictive/explanatory success warrant belief in unobservable posits?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REALISM, ABDUCTION_IBE, BAYESIAN_EPISTEMOLOGY present with no-miracles vs PMI

competency_questions.question: How do theory-ladenness and underdetermination limit evidence's decisiveness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THEORY_LADENNESS and UNDERDETERMINATION present with limit diagnosis

competency_questions.question: When evidence cannot decide between rival theories, what breaks the tie?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNDERDETERMINATION states tie-breaker strategy; RETRIEVAL grounds rivals

competency_questions.question: How do paradigms, normal science, anomalies, and crises structure scientific change?
Is theory change rational, and how do incommensurability and research programmes bear on it?
What is the target of belief: truth about unobservables or only empirical adequacy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REALISM vs ANTIREALISM_INSTRUMENTALISM conflict resolved via aim

competency_questions.question: Which model of explanation distinguishes genuine explanation from mere prediction?
What legitimate roles do epistemic and non-epistemic values play in theory choice?

glossary.definition: the property of a theory of being refutable by some possible observation
Popperian measure of how severely a theory has been tested and survived, without inductive support
ampliative inference from observed cases to unobserved cases or general laws
inference to the best explanation of the evidence
a shared constellation of exemplars, methods, and commitments guiding normal science
absence of a common measure or fully shared language/standards between successive paradigms
a Lakatosian sequence of theories with a hard core, protective belt, and heuristics
the view that successful theories are approximately true and their unobservables exist
the view that science aims only at empirical adequacy, with acceptance not belief about unobservables
the situation in which evidence does not uniquely fix a theory among rivals
the dependence of observation and data on theoretical commitments
the deductive-nomological account explaining an event by deducing it from laws and conditions

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established philosophy-of-science literature (incl. Popper 1959, Kuhn 1962) and scholarly practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Specify what an inquiry seeks (truth, empirical adequacy, understanding, prediction, control) before any method or appraisal rule is chosen.

included: aim selection (truth vs empirical adequacy vs understanding)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when stakeholders reveal the inquiry actually targets control/prediction rather than truth

pros.claim: frames every downstream method and appraisal choice
pros.example: a forecasting task picks empirical adequacy, not realist truth, as its aim

cons.claim: aim disputes are partly philosophical and can stall operational work
cons.example: truth-vs-adequacy debate delays method selection

failure_modes: implicit aim mismatched with chosen method

nodes.definition: Assess whether and how generalizing from observed to unobserved cases or to laws can be justified given Hume's problem.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a proposed inductive justification is shown circular or grue-vulnerable

pros.claim: clarifies the unavoidable inductive risk in any empirical generalization
pros.example: predicting the next swan's color exposes the uniformity assumption

cons.claim: no fully non-circular justification of induction is agreed
cons.example: appeals to induction's past success beg the question

acceptance_tests: circularity of any justification is checked
revisit_triggers: shift from enumerative to ampliative inference

nodes.definition: Use truth-preserving deductive structure to derive testable consequences and check validity and soundness of arguments and theories.
contradictors: holist denying clean deductive test isolation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a derivation is found to smuggle hidden auxiliary premises

pros.claim: truth-preserving and makes hidden assumptions explicit
pros.example: modus tollens lets a failed prediction bear on a theory

cons.claim: valid does not mean true; soundness needs separate evidence
cons.example: a valid argument from false premises proves nothing about the world

nodes.definition: Select the hypothesis that, if true, would best explain the evidence, using explanatory virtues as the inference criterion.
contradictors: van Fraassen-style critic of IBE (bad-lot objection)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the candidate set is shown incomplete (bad-lot objection bites)

pros.claim: models actual theory choice better than pure deduction
pros.example: Darwin argued natural selection best explained biogeography and homology

cons.claim: the best of a bad lot need not be true; virtue weighting is contestable
cons.example: the simplest explanation can be false if the true one was never considered

failure_modes: assuming the true hypothesis is in the candidate set
acceptance_tests: explanatory virtues are made explicit and weighted

nodes.definition: Apply Popper's method: advance bold falsifiable conjectures, expose them to severe tests, and reject those refuted.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when Duhem-Quine holism blocks pinning a refutation on the target hypothesis

pros.claim: prioritizes risky, testable theories and guards against ad hoc rescue
pros.example: Eddington's 1919 eclipse test was a genuine potential falsifier of general relativity

cons.claim: naive falsification ignores that auxiliaries can always absorb refutation
cons.example: an anomaly can be blamed on instruments rather than the core theory

acceptance_tests: at least one concrete potential falsifier is specified
test severity is argued (not easy to pass)

nodes.definition: Track how well a theory has survived severe tests (corroboration) without treating survival as inductive confirmation of future success.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when corroboration is silently used to predict future reliability

pros.claim: a non-inductive way to compare surviving theories
pros.example: relativity is better corroborated than Newton after passing harder tests

cons.claim: corroboration gives no forward-looking warrant, limiting practical use
cons.example: high corroboration cannot justify betting on tomorrow's prediction

acceptance_tests: severity of each passed test is recorded
no inductive leap from corroboration to prediction

nodes.definition: Define and apply confirmation relations between evidence and hypotheses while handling paradoxes (raven, tacking).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a confirmation rule generates a paradox (e.g. confirms via irrelevant conjuncts)

pros.claim: makes evidential support relations precise and criticizable
pros.example: instance confirmation clarifies when a black raven supports 'all ravens are black'

cons.claim: classic paradoxes show naive instance rules are unstable
cons.example: raven paradox: a white shoe trivially confirms the raven hypothesis

failure_modes: adopting an instance rule that licenses the raven/tacking paradox
acceptance_tests: chosen rule is tested against raven and tacking cases

nodes.definition: Represent belief as probability and update by conditionalization using priors, likelihoods, and Bayes factors to model evidential support.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when prior sensitivity or the problem of old evidence undermines a conclusion

pros.claim: gives a precise, general model of incremental support and updating
pros.example: a positive test raises a hypothesis's posterior via its Bayes factor

cons.claim: prior choice, old evidence, and logical omniscience remain open problems
cons.example: two agents with different priors can rationally diverge on the same data

failure_modes: hiding subjective priors as if objective
ignoring the problem of old evidence
acceptance_tests: priors are stated and sensitivity is checked

nodes.definition: Account for how observation, measurement, and data are shaped by theoretical commitments rather than being theory-neutral.
contradictors: logical empiricist seeking a neutral observation language

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a supposedly neutral measurement is shown to presuppose the theory under test

pros.claim: prevents naive appeals to 'just the data' as a neutral arbiter
pros.example: reading a thermometer presupposes thermodynamic theory

cons.claim: strong ladenness threatens the objectivity of test outcomes
cons.example: if all data are laden, rival theories may never confront shared evidence

acceptance_tests: theoretical presuppositions of key measurements are listed
degree of shared lower-level base is assessed
revisit_triggers: measurement procedure presupposes the target theory

nodes.definition: Diagnose when evidence is consistent with multiple incompatible theories, distinguishing transient from in-principle underdetermination.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when alleged empirical equivalence dissolves under new measurements or virtue-based tie-breaking

pros.claim: forces explicit non-empirical tie-breakers when data cannot decide
pros.example: conventionalist alternatives to relativity were empirically equivalent

cons.claim: strong in-principle underdetermination is hard to establish and often overstated
cons.example: most alleged equivalent rivals are eventually distinguished by new evidence

failure_modes: ignoring that auxiliaries differ between rivals
acceptance_tests: empirical-equivalence claim is argued, not assumed

nodes.definition: Provide criteria distinguishing science from non-science/pseudoscience and apply them to contested claims.
contradictors: Laudan-style skeptic of any sharp demarcation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a single criterion misclassifies a clear science/pseudoscience case

pros.claim: guards inquiry against unfalsifiable, immunized claims
pros.example: astrology fails because it makes no risky, refutable predictions

cons.claim: no single criterion cleanly separates all science from non-science
cons.example: early-stage legitimate theories can look unfalsifiable

acceptance_tests: criterion tested on agreed paradigm and pseudoscience cases

nodes.definition: Model Kuhnian normal science: puzzle-solving within a shared paradigm of exemplars, methods, and disciplinary matrix.
contradictors: Popperian seeing normal science as uncritical dogmatism

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when accumulating anomalies signal a transition from normal science toward crisis

pros.claim: explains the productive, convergent character of mature research
pros.example: 19th-century physics solved puzzles inside the Newtonian paradigm

cons.claim: can mask uncritical dogmatism and resistance to anomalies
cons.example: normal science may dismiss genuine refuting evidence as a mere puzzle

acceptance_tests: the paradigm's exemplars and shared methods are identified

nodes.definition: Identify when persistent anomalies undermine a paradigm and precipitate crisis, separating tolerable puzzles from paradigm-threatening anomalies.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a tolerated anomaly becomes paradigm-threatening or is resolved within the paradigm

pros.claim: distinguishes routine puzzles from paradigm-threatening anomalies
pros.example: Mercury's perihelion shift was an anomaly Newtonian physics could not absorb

cons.claim: anomaly/crisis judgments are partly retrospective and sociological
cons.example: whether a result counts as crisis-inducing is contested in real time

failure_modes: over-reading a single anomaly as crisis
acceptance_tests: anomaly persistence and breadth are documented

nodes.definition: Analyze paradigm shifts and the incommensurability (semantic, methodological, perceptual) between successive paradigms.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when alleged incommensurability is shown to permit partial translation and rational comparison

pros.claim: explains why paradigm debates are not simple point-by-point refutations
pros.example: 'mass' shifts meaning between Newtonian and relativistic frameworks

cons.claim: strong incommensurability threatens scientific rationality and progress
cons.example: if paradigms cannot be compared, theory choice looks non-rational

failure_modes: inferring total untranslatability from local meaning shift
using incommensurability to deny progress entirely
acceptance_tests: which terms/standards shift is specified, not asserted globally

nodes.definition: Appraise theories as research programmes with a hard core, protective belt, and heuristics, judged progressive or degenerating.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a programme starts predicting novel facts (progressive) or only absorbing anomalies (degenerating)

pros.claim: appraises a series of theories over time, not single refutations
pros.example: the Newtonian programme was progressive while predicting Neptune

cons.claim: progressive/degenerating labels are often clear only in hindsight
cons.example: a temporarily stagnant programme may later recover

failure_modes: abandoning a programme on a single anomaly
protecting a degenerating core with ad hoc moves
acceptance_tests: the hard core and protective belt are identified
the novel-prediction track record is assessed
revisit_triggers: a novel prediction succeeds or fails

nodes.definition: Evaluate the claim that successful theories are approximately true and that their unobservable posits genuinely exist.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the pessimistic meta-induction or underdetermination weakens the success-to-truth inference

pros.claim: explains predictive success as no miracle if theories are approximately true
pros.example: atomic theory's novel predictions suggest atoms really exist

cons.claim: pessimistic meta-induction: many past successful theories were false
cons.example: phlogiston and ether were predictively useful yet non-referring

failure_modes: inferring truth directly from success (ignoring PMI)
acceptance_tests: the success-to-truth inference is defended against PMI
the scope of realist commitment is specified
revisit_triggers: reference of a key term fails

nodes.definition: Develop and weigh anti-realist alternatives (constructive empiricism, instrumentalism) aiming at empirical adequacy or usefulness rather than truth about unobservables.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the observable/unobservable line is shown unprincipled or empirical adequacy collapses into realism

pros.claim: avoids over-committing belief to ever-revisable unobservable posits
pros.example: one can use quantum theory without believing a literal wavefunction collapse

cons.claim: the observable/unobservable distinction is hard to draw principledly
cons.example: why trust microscopes but not the entities they reveal?

acceptance_tests: acceptance vs belief is kept distinct

nodes.definition: Select and apply an account of scientific explanation (deductive-nomological, statistical-relevance, causal, mechanistic, unificationist).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when DN counterexamples (flagpole, irrelevance) force a causal/mechanistic account

pros.claim: distinguishes genuine explanation from mere prediction or correlation
pros.example: DN subsumes events under laws; causal accounts add the why-direction

cons.claim: classic counterexamples defeat the DN model's sufficiency
cons.example: the flagpole/shadow case shows DN ignores explanatory asymmetry

acceptance_tests: the chosen model handles flagpole and irrelevance cases

nodes.definition: Assess the roles of epistemic and non-epistemic values in theory choice, inductive risk, and the value-free ideal.
contradictors: defender of the strict value-free ideal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when non-epistemic values are shown to (illegitimately) determine evidence appraisal itself

pros.claim: shows accept/reject thresholds depend on the costs of error (inductive risk)
pros.example: setting a drug's significance threshold reflects the harm of false approval

cons.claim: unconstrained value influence risks bias and wishful thinking
cons.example: letting preferred conclusions set evidential standards corrupts inquiry

acceptance_tests: legitimate vs illegitimate value roles are distinguished

nodes.definition: Locate, retrieve, and critically appraise authoritative philosophy-of-science sources (primary texts, SEP/IEP, peer literature) for a given question.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a relied-upon source is a contested interpretation rather than a primary or consensus claim

pros.claim: anchors claims to primary texts (Popper 1959, Kuhn 1962) and vetted literature
pros.example: tracing 'falsifiability' to The Logic of Scientific Discovery rather than a blog summary

cons.claim: interpretive disputes mean source authority is itself contestable
cons.example: SEP entries summarize but cannot settle live interpretive debates

failure_modes: citing a secondary summary as primary doctrine
acceptance_tests: primary vs secondary sources are labeled
at least one authoritative source per major claim
revisit_triggers: source revealed as a contested interpretation

edges.why_related: the chosen epistemic aim determines whether ampliative inductive risk is acceptable
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligning inference mode with aim avoids rework
edges.risk_of_conflict: aim drift forces re-justifying inference
edges.example: truth-aim raises the bar on inductive justification
edges.resolution_rule: fix the aim before debating induction's justification

edges.why_related: aim selection fixes which test-consequences must be derived
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a clear aim makes derivation targets concrete
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unstated aim yields aimless derivations
edges.example: a control-aim emphasizes deriving actionable predictions
edges.resolution_rule: set the aim before building derivations

edges.why_related: what counts as a legitimate scientific aim shapes the demarcation criterion
edges.risk_of_conflict: aimless demarcation becomes arbitrary
edges.example: a truth-and-testability aim motivates falsifiability
edges.resolution_rule: ground demarcation in the inquiry's aim

edges.why_related: aims frame which puzzle-solving counts as progress within a paradigm
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping aim muddles puzzle valuation
edges.example: a prediction aim shapes which puzzles matter
edges.resolution_rule: state aims before characterizing normal science

edges.why_related: whether truth is the aim is prior to claiming theories are approximately true
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating aim and metaphysics causes confusion
edges.example: a truth-aim is presupposed by realism
edges.resolution_rule: resolve the aim before adopting realism

edges.why_related: epistemic aims define which values count as epistemic
edges.risk_of_conflict: unclear aim blurs the epistemic/non-epistemic line
edges.example: a truth-aim privileges accuracy as an epistemic value
edges.resolution_rule: fix the aim before adjudicating value roles

edges.why_related: the inquiry's aim sets relevance criteria for which sources are authoritative
edges.risk_of_conflict: sourcing without aim retrieves irrelevant material
edges.example: a truth-aim prioritizes primary canonical texts
edges.resolution_rule: define the aim before retrieval

edges.why_related: confirmation theory presupposes a stance on the legitimacy of inductive support
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring induction destabilizes confirmation
edges.example: Hume's problem motivates confirmation-paradox handling
edges.resolution_rule: address induction before formal confirmation

edges.why_related: Bayesian confirmation is one formal solution to confirmation-theory problems
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping confirmation issues yields naive Bayes use
edges.example: a Bayes factor resolves the raven paradox quantitatively
edges.resolution_rule: resolve qualitative confirmation before quantifying

edges.why_related: the induction problem motivates probabilistic models of ampliative inference
edges.benefit_of_coupling: ordering links inductive risk to credence updating
edges.risk_of_conflict: using Bayes without the induction context hides priors' role
edges.example: convergence theorems are a Bayesian reply to Hume
edges.resolution_rule: frame induction before Bayesian updating

edges.why_related: IBE relies on deriving the explanatory consequences each hypothesis would have
edges.risk_of_conflict: weak derivation corrupts best-explanation ranking
edges.example: deriving predicted observations lets IBE rank rivals
edges.resolution_rule: secure derivations before comparing explanations

edges.why_related: the no-miracles argument for realism is itself an inference to the best explanation
edges.risk_of_conflict: unexamined IBE makes realism rest on a weak base
edges.example: truth best explains predictive success (no-miracles)
edges.resolution_rule: appraise IBE's reliability before grounding realism on it

edges.why_related: the DN model of explanation is built from deductive subsumption under laws
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring derivation breaks DN adequacy
edges.example: DN explains by deducing the explanandum from laws plus conditions
edges.resolution_rule: establish derivation before DN explanation

edges.why_related: the explanatory virtues used in IBE depend on the adopted model of explanation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligning IBE with the explanation model is coherent
edges.risk_of_conflict: mismatched models make virtue talk vague
edges.example: a mechanistic model reshapes what counts as the best explanation
edges.resolution_rule: pick the explanation model alongside IBE criteria

edges.why_related: Popper's falsifiability is simultaneously a demarcation criterion and a method
edges.benefit_of_coupling: demarcation choice fixes the falsificationist method
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating them separately causes inconsistency
edges.example: falsifiability demarcates and prescribes severe testing
edges.resolution_rule: settle the demarcation criterion before applying falsificationism

edges.why_related: corroboration is defined only within the falsificationist appraisal scheme
edges.risk_of_conflict: using corroboration without it invites inductive misreading
edges.example: a theory is corroborated by surviving severe tests
edges.resolution_rule: fix the falsificationist framework before scoring corroboration

edges.why_related: Lakatos's programmes are a sophisticated revision of naive falsificationism
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping the lineage obscures why programmes arose
edges.example: programmes replace single-test falsification with series appraisal
edges.resolution_rule: understand falsificationism before its Lakatosian repair

edges.why_related: anomalies and crisis are defined relative to an established paradigm's expectations
edges.risk_of_conflict: without the paradigm, anomalies cannot be identified
edges.example: Mercury's perihelion is anomalous only given Newtonian expectations
edges.resolution_rule: characterize the paradigm before diagnosing anomalies

edges.why_related: crisis driven by anomalies is the precondition for a revolutionary paradigm shift
edges.benefit_of_coupling: crisis analysis sets up revolution analysis
edges.risk_of_conflict: analyzing revolution without crisis is ungrounded
edges.example: sustained crisis precipitated the relativistic revolution
edges.resolution_rule: diagnose crisis before modeling revolution

edges.why_related: programme appraisal reinterprets anomalies as degeneration signals rather than crises
edges.benefit_of_coupling: linking them clarifies rival change models
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating the two muddles appraisal
edges.example: a degenerating programme keeps absorbing anomalies ad hoc
edges.resolution_rule: compare crisis vs degeneration accounts explicitly

edges.why_related: ladenness of data strengthens underdetermination by weakening neutral evidence
edges.benefit_of_coupling: linking them clarifies the anti-realist case
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating data as neutral hides underdetermination
edges.example: laden measurements may not break a theory tie
edges.resolution_rule: assess ladenness before claiming underdetermination

edges.why_related: both express limits on how far evidence fixes ampliative conclusions
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them double-counts the same gap
edges.example: Duhem-Quine holism compounds inductive risk
edges.resolution_rule: treat induction and underdetermination as distinct limits

edges.why_related: what one accepts as genuine explanation shapes the explanatory argument for realism
edges.risk_of_conflict: mismatch weakens the no-miracles argument
edges.example: causal explanation strengthens entity realism
edges.resolution_rule: fix the explanation model before leaning on it for realism

edges.why_related: new authoritative sources can trigger revisiting the realism appraisal
edges.risk_of_conflict: without it, stances ossify against new scholarship
edges.example: a new historical case study revives the pessimistic induction
edges.resolution_rule: revisit realism when a cited source is superseded; stop when no new authoritative source bears on it

edges.why_related: primary-text retrieval can trigger correcting popular misreadings of falsificationism
edges.risk_of_conflict: without it, naive readings persist
edges.example: Popper's actual view is subtler than 'one refutation kills a theory'
edges.resolution_rule: revisit the falsificationism node when a primary text contradicts a secondary summary; stop once grounded in primary sources

edges.why_related: realism and anti-realism give incompatible answers about belief in unobservables
edges.benefit_of_coupling: forcing the contrast sharpens the aim debate
edges.risk_of_conflict: unresolved, it destabilizes every truth-claim's scope
edges.example: no-miracles (realist) vs pessimistic-induction (anti-realist)
edges.resolution_rule: resolve via the declared epistemic aim: a truth-aim favors realism, an adequacy-aim favors anti-realism

edges.why_related: underdetermination challenges realism by allowing empirically equivalent false rivals
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignored, realism overclaims from success
edges.example: empirically equivalent rivals to a 'true' theory undercut no-miracles
edges.resolution_rule: resolve by demonstrating evidence/virtue-based discrimination of rivals; if none, downgrade realist commitment

edges.why_related: Popperian corroboration explicitly rejects the Bayesian probabilistic confirmation it competes with
edges.risk_of_conflict: mixing them yields incoherent appraisal
edges.example: corroboration denies, Bayes asserts, forward-looking support
edges.resolution_rule: choose one appraisal framework per analysis and state which; never mix corroboration with posterior probability

edges.why_related: Duhem-Quine underdetermination undermines naive falsification's clean refutations
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignored, falsification overclaims decisiveness
edges.example: a refutation can be blamed on auxiliaries, not the core
edges.resolution_rule: accept holism: target a refutation only after auxiliary review (sophisticated falsificationism)

edges.why_related: incommensurability and Kuhn-loss challenge the cumulative approximate-truth claim of realism
edges.benefit_of_coupling: explicit tension forces a progress account
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignored, realism assumes smooth convergence
edges.example: reference shifts across paradigms threaten cross-theory truth
edges.resolution_rule: defend partial reference / structural continuity to reconcile progress with revolution

edges.why_related: Bayesians and explanationists dispute whether explanatory virtue adds confirmation beyond likelihoods
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflation hides the bonus-for-explanation debate
edges.example: does 'best explanation' earn an extra probability boost?
edges.resolution_rule: treat explanatory virtue as a heuristic for priors/likelihoods unless an extra-evidential role is justified

edges.why_related: value-laden theory choice constrains how cleanly success can be read as truth
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring values inflates objectivity claims
edges.example: social values in theory acceptance complicate no-miracles
edges.resolution_rule: bracket non-epistemic values when assessing truth-aimed claims; record any residual value influence

edges.why_related: value commitments create pressure on where the science/non-science line is drawn
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmarked values distort demarcation
edges.example: value-driven dismissal of a field as 'unscientific'
edges.resolution_rule: keep demarcation criteria epistemic; flag and justify any value-based exclusion

edges.why_related: perceptual/semantic ladenness is a source of incommensurability across paradigms
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-stating it makes all observation paradigm-private
edges.example: Kuhn: scientists in different paradigms 'see' different things
edges.resolution_rule: bound ladenness to specific terms to limit incommensurability claims

edges.why_related: a paradigm trains perception and so ladens its practitioners' observations
edges.benefit_of_coupling: linking them grounds Kuhnian observation claims
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-reading makes observation wholly paradigm-bound
edges.example: trained physicists 'see' a pendulum where Aristotelians 'see' constrained fall
edges.resolution_rule: limit paradigm-induced ladenness to interpretation, not all perception

edges.why_related: anti-realism constrains explanation to observable regularities, limiting unobservable-positing models
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmarked, anti-realists smuggle in realist explanation
edges.example: constructive empiricists accept theories as empirically adequate, not as explanatory of unobservables
edges.resolution_rule: when anti-realist, restrict explanatory commitment to the observable

edges.why_related: both are rival post-Popperian accounts of large-scale theory change
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating them as identical loses key differences
edges.example: Lakatos vs Kuhn on the rationality of change
edges.resolution_rule: compare, do not merge, the programme and revolution accounts

edges.why_related: both appraise theories over evidence via different (probabilistic vs programmatic) lenses
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a sparse link aids cross-framework mapping
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-linking conflates distinct appraisal logics
edges.example: novel-fact prediction matters to both confirmation and programmes
edges.resolution_rule: keep as comparison only; do not treat as a dependency

edges.why_related: both relate evidence to hypothesis support, one via instances/probability and one via explanation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a sparse link supports inference-mode mapping
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-linking hides that IBE is ampliative beyond instance confirmation
edges.example: both bear on why evidence supports a hypothesis
edges.resolution_rule: keep as comparison; route inference choice through the aim, not by merging

conflict_axes.trigger: deciding whether to believe a theory's unobservable posits or only accept it as empirically adequate
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the declared epistemic aim dominates: truth-aim -> realism, adequacy-aim -> anti-realism
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if aim is genuinely undecided and stakes are high

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing whether evidence can positively support a generalization or only deductively refute it
resolution_order: assess whether ampliative support is needed
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for risky prediction, deductive falsifiability dominates; for theory selection, controlled ampliative inference is allowed with explicit risk
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a claim needs positive support deduction cannot supply

conflict_axes.trigger: appraising a surviving theory: corroboration record vs posterior probability
resolution_order: do not mix the two measures
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: do not mix frameworks; if forward-looking warrant is required, Bayesian confirmation dominates; if only past-test appraisal, corroboration suffices
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a decision needs predictive warrant corroboration cannot give

conflict_axes.trigger: a prediction fails: blame the core theory or an auxiliary/observation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: holism dominates naive falsification: never pin a refutation on the core before auxiliary review (sophisticated falsificationism)
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the refutation cannot be localized to any component
conflict_axes.example: Eddington data interpreted under contested auxiliaries

conflict_axes.trigger: whether to keep puzzle-solving within a paradigm or treat anomalies as refuting
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: tolerate anomalies while the paradigm is productive; escalate to crisis when anomalies are persistent, broad, and unresolved
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a productive paradigm is suppressing a decisive anomaly

conflict_axes.trigger: whether paradigm change is rational progress or an incommensurable gestalt switch
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: limit incommensurability to specific terms; rational appraisal via novel predictions and partial reference dominates a global non-comparability claim
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no shared standard or translation can be found
conflict_axes.example: Kuhn's gestalt switch vs Lakatos's progressive appraisal

conflict_axes.trigger: treating predictive/confirmational success as if it were explanatory adequacy
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: explanatory adequacy (asymmetry, relevance) dominates: a predictively successful model is not thereby explanatory
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a decision rests on explanation but only prediction is established
conflict_axes.example: flagpole case: height explains shadow, not vice versa

conflict_axes.trigger: how far non-epistemic values may legitimately enter theory choice
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: values may set acceptance thresholds via inductive risk but must not determine evidence appraisal; epistemic constraints dominate there
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if non-epistemic values reach the appraisal of evidence itself
conflict_axes.example: error-cost-driven significance thresholds in drug approval

conflict_axes.trigger: relying on observation as a neutral arbiter despite theory-ladenness
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: acknowledge ladenness but seek a shared observational base; confirmation/test claims must be qualified by ladenness, not abandoned
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no shared base survives for rival theories

edge_cases.trigger: modeling the realism/anti-realism tradeoff as a dependency instead of a conflict
edge_cases.detection_method: scan for edges whose 'why_related' states a tradeoff but whose edge_type is not conflict
resolution: reclassify as conflict edge with signed_tension<0

edge_cases.trigger: labeling a heuristic prior as observed or experimentally_validated
edge_cases.detection_method: grep value_labels/metric_labels for observed|experimentally_validated when no OBSERVED_DATA

edge_cases.trigger: edited a base metric without recomputing derived score fields
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute final_importance/risk_score/etc and diff against stored values (tol 0.02)

edge_cases.trigger: adding a dependency edge that creates a directed cycle
edge_cases.failure_mode: no valid topological order for priority_order
edge_cases.detection_method: run DFS cycle detection over dependency edges and node.dependencies
resolution: convert the weaker dependency to sequence/feedback

edge_cases.trigger: placing a dependent node before its prerequisite in priority_order
edge_cases.failure_mode: downstream work done before its foundation
edge_cases.detection_method: verify each node appears after all its dependencies in priority_order

edge_cases.trigger: a node with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 lacks acceptance_tests or human_review
edge_cases.detection_method: for each node with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 check non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true

edge_cases.trigger: a node with cross_topic_coupling>=0.75 lacks revisit_triggers
edge_cases.detection_method: for each node with cross_topic_coupling>=0.75 check non-empty revisit_triggers
resolution: add revisit_triggers tied to coupled nodes

edge_cases.trigger: template placeholder text survives into the populated KB
edge_cases.detection_method: scan raw JSON for the schema's reserved template tokens and template node-id stand-ins

edge_cases.trigger: an evidence_ref points to a source_id absent from source_registry
edge_cases.detection_method: check every evidence_ref resolves to a source_registry source_id
resolution: add the source record or fix the ref to SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR

edge_cases.trigger: inferring total untranslatability from a local meaning shift
edge_cases.detection_method: check incommensurability claims name specific shifted terms and offer a comparison strategy
resolution: scope the claim to specific terms

edge_cases.trigger: mixing corroboration and Bayesian posterior as if one measure
edge_cases.detection_method: check each appraisal states a single framework and does not combine corroboration with posterior probability

workflow.objective: fix the epistemic aim, claim scope, and authoritative source criteria
acceptance_tests: at least one primary source identified
workflow.do_first_because: the aim is the highest-coupling foundation every later appraisal depends on

workflow.objective: characterize the inference modes available and their risks
acceptance_tests: each mode's scope and limits stated
workflow.do_first_because: inference modes underpin both confirmation and appraisal steps

workflow.objective: set the science/non-science criterion and the testing method
acceptance_tests: at least one potential falsifier specified
exit_criteria: demarcation criterion and test method agreed
workflow.do_first_because: the testing method must precede appraisal of test outcomes

workflow.objective: establish how evidence confirms hypotheses and handle paradoxes
choose a theory-appraisal framework and apply it without mixing frameworks
entry_criteria: demarcation criterion and test method agreed
workflow.do_first_because: appraisal must not silently mix incompatible frameworks

workflow.objective: diagnose theory-ladenness and underdetermination affecting the evidence base
workflow.do_first_because: limits must be known before any realism/anti-realism conclusion

workflow.objective: model normal science, anomalies, crisis, and revolutionary change
workflow.do_first_because: high-coupling, high-risk node REVOLUTIONS_INCOMMENSURABILITY needs review before metaphysical commitment

workflow.objective: select and justify a model of scientific explanation
workflow.do_first_because: the explanation model feeds the no-miracles argument for realism

workflow.objective: settle the realism/anti-realism stance and the legitimate role of values
exit_criteria: metaphysical stance and value roles set
workflow.do_first_because: high-risk REALISM and the realism/anti-realism conflict require human review before commitment

workflow.objective: validate references, formulas, and grounding; produce the final handoff
entry_criteria: metaphysical stance and value roles set
exit_criteria: validation passed; ready for review-gated lock
workflow.do_first_because: validation and grounding must pass before any hard lock

dominance_rules.trigger: a quick conclusion risks an unsupported epistemic commitment
dominance_rules.rule: never accept a fast philosophical conclusion that fails grounding or acceptance tests
dominance_rules.required_action: block lock until acceptance tests and source grounding pass
dominance_rules.example: rushing to a realist verdict before addressing the pessimistic meta-induction is rejected

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node lacks a resolved prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: order by dependency precedence before risk-adjusted value
dominance_rules.example: REALISM cannot finalize before ABDUCTION_IBE and EPISTEMIC_AIMS

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric estimate is presented as more certain than its evidence
dominance_rules.rule: evidence label governs; do not imply observed certainty for heuristic priors
dominance_rules.required_action: keep all unsupported numbers labeled heuristic with observed fields at 0.0
dominance_rules.example: a confidence value stays heuristic because no dataset measured it

dominance_rules.trigger: validation has not passed but a lock is requested
dominance_rules.rule: QA dominates locking; no hard lock before validation passes
dominance_rules.required_action: require validator exit 0 and reference integrity before any lock
dominance_rules.example: the realism stance stays draft until formula and reference checks pass

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible commitment is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates for risk_if_wrong>=0.80 or irreversible stance commitments
dominance_rules.required_action: route high-risk nodes to human_review_required=true before finalization
dominance_rules.example: FALSIFICATIONISM and REALISM commitments require human review

dominance_rules.rule: schema stability dominates raw density; do not break structure to add nodes
dominance_rules.required_action: reject content that violates required object structure
dominance_rules.example: drop a near-duplicate node rather than corrupt node structure

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting conflicts with strict JSON validity
dominance_rules.rule: strict JSON validity dominates prose elegance
dominance_rules.required_action: emit machine-parsable JSON only, no markdown or commentary
dominance_rules.example: no explanatory prose is added outside the JSON object

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim lacks an authoritative source
dominance_rules.rule: source grounding dominates; cite primary/authoritative sources or downgrade the claim
dominance_rules.required_action: attach evidence_refs or qualify the claim as heuristic
dominance_rules.example: a falsificationism reading is corrected to match Popper 1959 primary text

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient ordering would introduce a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.rule: acyclicity dominates; convert the weaker dependency to sequence/feedback
dominance_rules.required_action: demote the weaker edge and record the repair
dominance_rules.example: RETRIEVAL->REALISM is modeled as feedback, not dependency, to avoid a cycle

dominance_rules.trigger: a single failed prediction is treated as a clean refutation
dominance_rules.rule: holism dominates naive falsification; review auxiliaries before blaming the core
dominance_rules.required_action: perform an auxiliary-assumption review before localizing a refutation
dominance_rules.example: an anomaly is provisionally blamed on instruments pending review

dominance_rules.trigger: the realism/anti-realism stance is asserted without a declared aim
dominance_rules.rule: the declared epistemic aim dominates the metaphysical stance choice
dominance_rules.required_action: resolve EPISTEMIC_AIMS before committing to realism or anti-realism
dominance_rules.example: an adequacy-aim inquiry adopts constructive empiricism, not realism

dominance_rules.trigger: non-epistemic values reach the appraisal of evidence
dominance_rules.rule: epistemic constraints dominate evidence appraisal; non-epistemic values may set only acceptance thresholds
dominance_rules.required_action: bracket non-epistemic values from evidence appraisal and record any threshold-setting role
dominance_rules.example: harm-of-error may set a significance threshold but not reinterpret the data

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve the epistemic aim before selecting inference or appraisal methods
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a method chosen against the wrong aim forces full rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: method selected before aim is fixed
anti_rework_rules.example: picking Bayesian appraisal before deciding the aim is truth vs adequacy

anti_rework_rules.rule: derive competency questions before populating nodes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: nodes without CQ targets drift and get rebuilt
anti_rework_rules.example: adding an explanation node with no CQ it answers

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the source registry before assigning evidence labels
anti_rework_rules.rationale: labels without sources become unresolved references
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: evidence_ref pointing to a missing source
anti_rework_rules.example: labeling a value observed before any dataset source exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: characterize inference modes before theory appraisal
anti_rework_rules.rationale: appraisal built on unclear inference logic must be redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: corroboration/Bayes used before inference modes are mapped
anti_rework_rules.example: scoring corroboration before deciding deduction-vs-induction roles

anti_rework_rules.rule: settle the demarcation criterion before applying severe testing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: testing under an unsettled criterion yields contested verdicts
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: falsification applied before a demarcation criterion is fixed
anti_rework_rules.example: calling a claim pseudoscience before stating the criterion

anti_rework_rules.rule: document theory-ladenness and underdetermination before any realism verdict
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a realism stance set before limits ignores its strongest objections
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: REALISM finalized before UNDERDETERMINATION is diagnosed
anti_rework_rules.example: asserting no-miracles before addressing empirically equivalent rivals

anti_rework_rules.rule: populate all metric variables before computing derived scores
anti_rework_rules.rationale: computing scores from missing variables forces recomputation
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a derived score present while a base metric is absent
anti_rework_rules.example: final_importance set before criticality is assigned

anti_rework_rules.rule: finalize node ids before building edges and references
anti_rework_rules.rationale: edges to renamed nodes break reference integrity
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an edge endpoint not in the node id set
anti_rework_rules.example: an edge to REALISM created before that node id is fixed

anti_rework_rules.rationale: a priority order built on cyclic/unmet deps must be rebuilt
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a node placed before its prerequisite in priority_order

anti_rework_rules.rule: identify conflict axes before writing dominance rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: dominance rules without mapped conflicts miss real tradeoffs
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a dominance rule with no corresponding conflict axis
anti_rework_rules.example: writing an aim-over-metaphysics rule before mapping the realism conflict

anti_rework_rules.rule: ensure acceptance tests and validation pass before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before tests forces a costly unlock-and-revalidate cycle
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a hard lock requested while validation_report has failures
anti_rework_rules.example: locking the realism stance before formula consistency passes

iteration_protocol.trigger: the validator or a check reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream impact
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold low-risk defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents and edges of the changed node
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set is stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.detection: map defect class to repair owner via repair_routing

iteration_protocol.trigger: a base metric or interval changed
iteration_protocol.detection: diff stored derived fields against formula output

iteration_protocol.stop_condition: validation passes with no new failures

iteration_protocol.trigger: new authoritative source bears on a node
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior change below the revisit delta (0.10)

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk defect cannot be auto-repaired
iteration_protocol.detection: check risk_if_wrong and irreversibility against thresholds

human_review_required_for: hard lock of any appraisal verdict

checks.repair_action: modeled RETRIEVAL->REALISM/FALSIFICATIONISM as feedback to avoid a cycle
recomputed all derived fields via the derivation script

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked stance change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
